A: At six, my daughter packed a suitcase to run away. She made it as far as the backyard, left a note that said 'back by dinner,' and took the good sandwiches. She has never once missed dinner since.
B: Grandad answers every message in the family group chat with a thumbs-up — good news, bad news, the argument about the will. Mum once asked if he even reads them. He sent a thumbs-up. She cried laughing.
C: Mum never changed her voicemail greeting. It is still my little sister at six, shouting 'Leave a message, we're probably eating!' — and every time it plays, the whole kitchen goes quiet for a second, then somebody laughs.
